paper.title: Accurate piezoelectric tensor prediction with equivariant attention tensor graph neural network
paper.research_summary: The paper proposes an equivariant attention tensor graph neural network (EATGNN) to predict the complete third-rank piezoelectric tensor for both bulk and two-dimensional materials, leveraging irreducible decomposition to preserve crystal symmetry and achieve frame-independence. It validates the model on datasets from Materials Project, C2DB, and high-throughput DFT studies, then uses it to screen for new high-performance piezoelectric candidates, which are experimentally validated via DFPT calculations.

task.objective: accurately predict the complete third-rank piezoelectric tensor for crystalline materials
constraints: must be independent of reference frame
must satisfy index symmetry eijk = eikj
output_goal: full third-rank piezoelectric tensor in Voigt notation (3×6 matrix) or 3×3 matrix for 2D

evidence.text: we propose an equivariant attention tensor graph neural network (EATGNN) that can identify crystal symmetry and remain independent of the reference frame, ultimately enabling the accurate prediction of the complete third-rank piezoelectric tensor.

EATGNN can establish the relationship between crystal structures and their properties... Ultimately, the model outputs the piezoelectric tensor in its irreducible representation, which is then post-processed to obtain the target piezoelectric tensor.

stages.stage_goal: acquire piezoelectric tensor data for training and evaluation

evidence.text: The piezoelectric tensor data of bulk crystals in this work was obtained from the Materials Project21 and a recent high-throughput computational study on piezoelectric tensors24,30.
The piezoelectric tensor data of 2D materials was obtained from the C2DB database33,34, comprising a total of 1382 data points...

stages.stage_goal: clean dataset by removing outliers and enforcing symmetry consistency

evidence.text: Due to the presence of a signiﬁcant number of outliers in the piezoelectric tensors, we performed data resampling before applying machine learning techniques to prevent overﬁtting.

We examined all materials dataset to ensure that the target piezoelectric tensors are consistent with the material’s symmetry. Furthermore, we mathematically adjusted those piezoelectric tensors that did not conform to the material’s symmetry to be invariant under crystallographic symmetry operations.
after analyzing and removing some extreme outliers to prevent the model from learning an inaccurate data distribution, 1350 data points were retained...

stages.stage_goal: optimize model parameters to minimize prediction error on piezoelectric tensor

evidence.text: Networks are trained using a mean-squared-error loss function based on complete piezoelectric tensor: loss ¼ 1/N Σ_N n=0 Σ_i,j,k (e0_nijk − enijk)^2 / 27
We train this model with the AdamW optimizer44 to minimize the loss function with a mini-batch size of 16.

stages.stage_name_raw: performance evaluation using MAE and RMSE
stages.stage_goal: quantify prediction accuracy of piezoelectric tensor components

evidence.text: The Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of EATGNN on the test set are 0.154 C/m2 and 0.141 C/m2, respectively.
the RMSE and MAE of our model are 50.6 pC/m and 16.8 pC/m, respectively.

stages.stage_name_raw: screening bulk and 2D materials for large piezoelectricity
stages.stage_goal: identify candidate materials with high predicted piezoelectric response
stage_output: list of candidate materials with predicted |e_ij|_max

evidence.text: Our selection criteria are 1) out of the training datasets, 2) inversion asymmetry, 3) Egap > 0.1 eV, and 4) Nuc < 30 atoms.

stages.stage_goal: verify predicted piezoelectric tensors using first-principles calculations

evidence.text: Using our model, we identify several good candidates (See in Tables 3 and 4 and Supplementary Material), which are further validated using density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) calculations.
